key_insight: First-principles spin-orbit calculations show that chiral perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ have strong spin-split band edges, with NEA producing a larger valence-edge splitting and opposite spin textures for opposite molecular handedness.
engineering_relevance: These results help guide molecular and crystal-design choices for chiral perovskite optoelectronics where spin polarization, circular dichroism, and band-edge alignment matter.
method: Density functional first-principles calculations including spin-orbit coupling
Comparison of spin-split band structures for PEA- vs NEA-based one-dimensional chiral perovskites
Group-theoretical analysis of the nonsymmorphic space group $P2_12_12_1$ to explain degeneracies and band sticking
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced spin splitting near both valence-band maximum and conduction-band minimum, with stronger effective valence-edge splitting in ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ despite similar linear-in-$k$ coefficients.
watch_item: The findings are computational and symmetry-based, so device performance still depends on synthesis quality, structural stability, and how closely real samples match the idealized crystal models.
paper_title: First-principles calculations of spin-split bands in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$
